idiom_name: new Proxy(target, handler) with traps + Reflect forwarding
implementation_notes: new Proxy(target, handler) is a language built-in: the handler's traps interpose on the fundamental internal methods ([[Get]], [[Set]], [[HasProperty]], [[Delete]], [[Construct]] and more), so no forwarding class is needed and even property enumeration, `in`, function calls and construction can be intercepted. Reflect.get(target, prop, receiver) supplies the default forwarding semantics inside a trap, and an empty handler yields a no-op proxy. A hand-written wrapper (delegating methods and Object.defineProperty getters) is only worth it when you need an ordinary object with stable identity, or when private fields and internal slots must keep working; the built-in remains the default realization.
pitfalls: Proxy invariants are enforced: a trap that reports a different value for a non-writable, non-configurable target property throws a TypeError.
Private class fields (#x) and internal slots (Map, Date, DOM nodes) break through a proxy because the receiver is the proxy, not the target; methods must be re-bound to the target.
A proxy is a different object from the target: identity comparisons, WeakMap keys and structuredClone/JSON behavior diverge unless handled.
Traps sit on every property access and can deoptimize hot code paths; measure before proxying performance-critical objects.
